clue.text: A church is 27 28

definitions.note: the linked answers 27 and 28 together say the thing is a fish

parts.note: a, as in 'five pounds a head', means per

explanation.surface: A remark that some church is shady or dubious in its dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme answer at 27 and 28 reads SOMETHING FISHY, so 'is 27 28' means 'is a kind of fish'. 'A' stands for 'per', as in a price per head.
explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater species is a well-known fish, so it is literally something fishy.

clue.text: Train smoker is 27 28

definitions.meaning: a steam locomotive is called a ... in nursery language
a smoker is someone who puffs on a cigarette or pipe
the linked answers 27 and 28 together say the thing is a fish

explanation.surface: A train with a smoking passenger aboard is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: a puffer train, someone who puffs, and the puffer fish, which can inflate itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish slang for a steam engine, a person who puffs smoke, and the inflatable blowfish all share this name.

clue.text: To start to speak about neglecting book is 27 28

indicators.note: neglecting means leaving something out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to broach a subject is to begin to talk about it

explanation.surface: Raising a topic while ignoring a particular book is suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neglecting book' removes B from BROACH.
explanation.definitionFit: This silvery freshwater species of the carp family is a fish.

clue.text: It's python dancing that defines stage entertainer

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the words are rearranged here

explanation.surface: A snake charmer's performance where the python dances is what marks out the stage act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges the nine letters of ITS PYTHON.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts volunteers into a trance in front of an audience performs as a stage entertainer.

clue.text: Tense, odd bloke is 27 28

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
rum is old British slang for odd or strange
Peter is a man's name, standing for any bloke

explanation.surface: A tense, peculiar man is behaving suspiciously.
explanation.definitionFit: This name belongs to several sea species, so it is a fish as well as a horn player.

clue.text: Salesman holding bridge up is 27 28

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tout is someone who sells tickets or touts for business
BR is a dictionary abbreviation for bridge

explanation.surface: A salesman propping up a bridge is up to something dodgy.
explanation.walkthrough: BR for bridge is a dictionary abbreviation rarely seen outside crosswords; 'up' turns the combined TOBRUT, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flatfish prized at table is a sea fish.

clue.text: Relative not getting the French drunk straightened out?

indicators.note: not getting means doing without, so letters are removed

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
le is French for the
oiled is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: An uncle who skipped the French lessons got drunk, then sobered up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting the French' takes LE from UNCLE, leaving UNC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or spring that has been unwound is straightened out, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Request time to work on skirt?

parts.note: a plea is a request

explanation.surface: Someone asks for time to finish working on a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding fabric into regular creases is a typical job when making a skirt, hence the question mark.

clue.text: That rider getting thrown is not very good

indicators.note: a rider thrown from a horse is tumbled about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider who keeps falling off the horse is not much of a jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting thrown' rearranges THAT RIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something third-class in quality is mediocre, so not very good.

clue.text: Popular music, deep in sound, is 27 28

parts.note: rock is a genre of popular music
a bass voice or note is deep in pitch

explanation.surface: Popular music heavy on the low end strikes someone as suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American sunfish is a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Theatre friend's fine coming back for girl in 20s

indicators.note: coming back means the string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a pal is a friend; the 's is read as 'is'
F is an abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A theatre friend's fine is returned, apparently to a young woman of the twenties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' reverses REP + PAL + F as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable young women of the 1920s, with bobbed hair and jazz, were called by this name.

clue.text: Priest coming in to train wanting reduction of the belly

indicators.note: coming in to means entering, so one piece goes inside the other
wanting reduction means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to coach is to train
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A priest joins a training regime to slim his belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting reduction' leaves COAC; 'of the belly' is fair because coeliac is the medical adjective for the abdomen, not only the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Coeliac is the anatomical adjective for the abdominal cavity, so it means relating to the belly.

clue.text: Race expert losing to the organised

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racing tipster loses to a better-organised rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges LOSING TO THE. 'Race' means a people, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar who studies peoples and their cultures is an expert in human races.

clue.text: Repulsion of evil is 27 28

indicators.note: repulsion drives something back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bad means evil

explanation.surface: Something that repels evil is suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: This small flatfish of European coastal waters is a member of the plaice family, so it is a fish.

clue.text: River, in a short time, is 27 28

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bit is a short time, as in 'wait a bit'

explanation.surface: A river that seems fishy after only a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Brit is a name for young herring and sprats, the small fry eaten as whitebait, so it is fish.

clue.text: Books about (say) motorway verge describing wide edge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for book, so two of them give BB
a motorway is an example of a road, as '(say)' signals
a rim is a verge or edge

explanation.surface: Books on the subject of motorway verges describe a wide edge.
explanation.walkthrough: '(say)' marks motorway as one example of a road; 'about' sets BROADB around it, and 'describing' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brim is a hat with a wide brim, so it names that wide edge.

clue.text: Serial favouritism surrounding new Eurovision contestants?

indicators.note: surrounding means one piece goes round the other

parts.note: bias is favouritism

explanation.surface: Persistent favouritism toward newcomers at the Eurovision Song Contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts BIAS round N, giving BIANS. The question mark: Serbia enters Eurovision, so its people are contestants by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbia competes in Eurovision, so its nationals can be cast as the competitors there, a definition by example.

clue.text: Sculpture, when right, captures religious stance? On the contrary

indicators.note: captures means holds inside, so one piece goes into the other
on the contrary reverses the stated order, so the stance takes in the other piece

parts.note: a belief is a religious stance
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: A sculpture which, when right, embodies a religious attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, AS R would hold BELIEF; 'On the contrary' flips that, so BELIEF captures ASR.
explanation.definitionFit: Low relief is a sculptural form in which figures project only slightly from a flat background.

clue.text: Dangerous material in Paris is restricted by court orders

indicators.note: restricted by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ASBOs were British anti-social behaviour orders issued by courts
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Something hazardous in Paris is curbed by court orders.
explanation.walkthrough: ASBOs are anti-social behaviour orders, British court orders that restrict a person's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral used in insulation causes lung disease, so it is a hazardous substance.

clue.text: Relative with colic upset — vegetable?

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a relative

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative with a bout of colic is left like a vegetable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges COLIC to CCOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: This green brassica with clustered heads is a common vegetable.

clue.text: Speech-makers disconcerted with dodgy press coverage?

indicators.note: coverage means one piece covers, so it goes round the other
dodgy suggests something unreliable or bent, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: out can mean disconcerted, as in 'put out'

explanation.surface: Speakers are rattled by unreliable press reporting of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' makes SPERS, and 'coverage' wraps it round OUT; 'disconcerted' gives OUT through the sense of being put out.
explanation.definitionFit: People who spout hold forth at length, so they are speech-makers, often windy ones.

clue.text: Spot (in ocean) one that's 27 28, nothing less

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: less means minus, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a sole is a flatfish, so the linked answers' 'something fishy' gives it
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A spot in the ocean where one finds something suspicious, minus nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' removes O from SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a spot of land in the ocean.

clue.text: VIP British women in current concert

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a gig is a concert

explanation.surface: A very important person: British women performing at a current concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts W inside IGIG, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An important, influential person is informally called by this name.

clue.text: Approximate variable in calculation is 27 28

parts.note: rough means approximate
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An approximate variable in a calculation is suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: This Australasian sea creature, also called a slimehead, is a fish.

clue.text: Tear drops lead to regret — stop

indicators.note: drops means loses, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to rend is to tear

indicators.note: the lead to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Tears fall, leading to regret, then stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is the verb to rip, not a teardrop, and 'drops' is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop is a synonym when used as a noun or verb meaning a finish or to finish.

clue.text: A little wind blowing back during exercise of oar in watery domain

indicators.note: during means inside, so the pieces sit within the other
exercise of means the letters are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: a chip is a little piece of something

indicators.note: blowing back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A light wind blowing back as a rower exercises the oar on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blowing back' makes ELAG and 'exercise of' makes AR_O; 'during' sets CHIPELAG in its gap. 'A little' is a chip, not the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea scattered with many islands is an area dominated by water.

clue.text: A poor service receiving regulator's first warning

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A weak tennis serve draws the umpire's first warning.
explanation.walkthrough: A let in tennis is a serve clipping the net, which must be replayed.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm signal or alert is a warning of danger.

clue.text: I'm held up by fool wrongly

indicators.note: held means contained, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: I'm gives the letters IM, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone complains they are being wrongly delayed by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes MI and 'held' sets it inside the fool; 'held up' looks like one phrase meaning delayed, but splits into two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Going amiss means going wrong, so the adverb means wrongly or astray.

clue.text: Trooped out for 27 28

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers trooped out to deal with something suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric ray, a flat sea creature that stuns prey, is also called by this name, so it is a fish.

clue.text: Old politician seizing money is 27 28

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Whigs were members of an old British party, forerunner of the Liberals
tin is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A former politician grabbing cash seems suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: This member of the cod family, common in British waters, is a sea fish.

clue.text: Satisfied with greeting in Carol's embrace: an indefinable feeling

indicators.note: embrace means hold round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a carol is a song
met means satisfied, as in 'met the demand'
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: Pleased by a hello while in Carol's arms, someone feels a vague emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name, but a carol is a song. 'with' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying there is 'a certain something' names an unspecified quality or sensation that resists description.

clue.text: Suspicious following attempt to secure 'Independent'

indicators.note: to secure means to hold inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, as in coconut shy

explanation.surface: The newspaper's own name appears in a suspicious attempt to secure it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' puts I between F and SHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious or questionable makes people doubtful of it.
